traits.habitat_notes: Maritime rocks, cliffs, sandy bluffs and dunes, salt marshes; inland on gravelly tundra, flood plains and alpine meadows (FNA subspecies; Wikipedia).

taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form chosen from the plant's habit: a dense tuft of grass-like leaves with many leafless scapes, each topped by a round pink head.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species.

allometry.note: 0.54 m tall at 4 years in the open, inside the floras' range of heights, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Every look comes from the characters through the library's rules: a dense tuft of grass-like leaves with many leafless scapes, each topped by a round pink head.

traits.library_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): perennial scapose herbs: forb.

traits.life_span.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs, perennial.

traits.woodiness.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): herbs with a branched woody rootstock.

traits.leaf_habit.note: English Wikipedia, Armeria maritima (read 2026-10-19): a compact evergreen perennial growing in low clumps.

traits.rosette.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves in basal rosettes; rootstock erect (species).

traits.cauline_leaves.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes leafless.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes erect, 2-60 cm, the full range kept as low and high; a usual 10-30 cm is an estimate within it (confidence medium).

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes to 60 cm.

traits.crown_width_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: old clumps of many rosettes from a branched rootstock reach about 30 cm across.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves alternate, spiralled.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves spiralled.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blades 1-15 cm x 0.5-3 mm: linear (genus linear to linear-spatulate).

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blades 1-15 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaf blades 0.5-3 mm wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): leaves sessile.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): margins entire.

traits.leaf_venation.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): blade base 1- or more or less 3-veined.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): faces glabrous or hairy (subsp. californica, sibirica either; interior glabrous).

traits.leaf_posture.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: the grass-like leaves spread and arch out from the rosette into a dense tuft.

traits.leaf_colour.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: no flora read names the leaf colour; a dark green to grey-green, sRGB by eye.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): solitary dense hemispheric heads.

traits.inflorescence_posture.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes erect.

traits.peduncle_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): scapes (the bare stalk of the head) 2-60 cm.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): heads 13-28 mm across (a hemispheric head, its depth less; diameter given).

traits.bract_form.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): involucre of scarious bracts.

traits.bract_length_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): outermost involucral bract ovate to triangular-lanceolate, 4-14 mm; involucral sheath below the head 5-32 mm.

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: a 13-28 mm head of several scorpioid cymes holds a few dozen flowers.

traits.flower_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): corolla pink to white; Wikipedia: bright pink, sometimes purple, white or red; sRGB by eye for 'pink'.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: no flora gives a flower size; each flower about 6-9 mm across, several to a 13-28 mm head.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): sepals 5, petals 5, stamens 5.

traits.perianth.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx tube and 5 petals.

traits.corolla_shape.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): petals only slightly joined at the base, so the limbs spread: rotate (an estimate of the open posture; FNA gives no corolla form).

traits.calyx_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): calyx funnel-shaped, 10-ribbed, its limb membranous (dry, papery, whitish); sRGB by eye for a papery white.

traits.stamens.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Plumbaginaceae family account (Morin) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): stamens 5.

traits.carpels.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): styles 5.

traits.fruit_type.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits dry, enclosed in the persistent calyx, opening transversely; read as capsule.

traits.calyx_in_fruit.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria (Lefebvre & Vekemans) (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): fruits enclosed in persistent calyces.

traits.flowering_months.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): subspecies: californica mid spring-mid summer, maritima late spring-early summer, sibirica and interior summer; together April-August. Wikipedia: British salt marshes April-October.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence low), as no source read gives it: fruits ripen within the papery calyx a month or so after flowering, June to September.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): subspecies from 0 m.

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): subsp. sibirica to 1200 m.

traits.light.note: English Wikipedia, Armeria maritima (read 2026-10-19): coastal cliffs, grassland and salt marshes, mountain rocks: open sites.

traits.moisture.note: English Wikipedia, Armeria maritima (read 2026-10-19): dry, sandy, saline conditions.

traits.soil_texture.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): maritime rocks, cliffs, sandy bluffs and dunes, gravel pavements.

traits.habitat_notes.note: Flora of North America vol. 5 (2005), Armeria maritima (eFloras, read 2026-10-19): habitats of the four North American subspecies; Wikipedia adds salt marshes and copper- and lead-rich soils.

traits.rosette_leaves.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: a dense cushion of many crowded rosettes of narrow leaves (Flora of China: leaves crowded in a basal tuft), each rosette round one scape.

traits.flowering_stems.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read counts it: each rosette of the cushion sends up a scape, so a plant carries many.
